item.title: Safety as Distance to a Boundary: A Control-Barrier Framework for Agent Trajectories
item.description: One formal framework for the safety of an LLM agent's trajectory, built on control barrier functions: an abstract state of the observed trace, a scalar barrier h whose sign is safety and whose value is the margin, a one-step invariance condition that is the only source of a guarantee, min-composition with blame by argmin, a least-restrictive filter with a fallback, an explicit fidelity band for the abstraction error, and an adversary written as parameters. Three routes instantiate it: symbolic-compiled, environment-driven, semantic-learned. Every step is set beside its counterpart in autonomous driving (RSS, Safety Force Field, Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, STL).

item.title: Can We Imitate the Steps by Which Humans Understand the World?
item.description: A formal model for auto-research: an explicit state (working graph + joint posterior over a frozen candidate space), actions with frozen observation models chosen by expected information gain per cost, Bayes updates from verified evidence only, a separate gate for adopting a graph, an explicit branch for widening the hypothesis space, and a sealed, replayable end. Written out as three loops: reading, probing, benchmarking.

item.title: Lifelong Learning, Formally: Objects, Boundaries, Schools
item.description: A three-layer formalisation of lifelong learning: the mathematical objects (a hidden generator with a variation budget, regimes, an agent of bounded size, what its policy really holds, a bounded-capacity oracle, dynamic regret), three criteria that separate lifelong learning from eight neighbouring paradigms, and twelve schools of existing method sorted by the three challenges they answer. With the lineage of every piece, and a note on why survival, not regret, is the real score.

item.title: A Company in a Box: physics, a server sandbox, and a two-tier agent team
item.description: A closed-loop sandbox for evaluating LLM agent teams that run a business: a street-level world, a server with a real deploy pipeline, one ledger that pays for everything, and a three-role team with locked permissions. With the four-layer replay of one run, and an essay on what it means to let an agent team run a company.

item.title: Cognitive Operators: Building a Capability Benchmark with No Ceiling
item.description: An interactive atlas of 27 cognitive operators run on 9 frontier LLMs across 3 families: which probes show a capability cliff everywhere, which ones were only measuring in-context lookup, and why operator construction is the core input to harness design.

item.title: Limits from Task Partitioning and Communication Bottlenecks
item.description: A plain-language walk through our paper on the information-theoretic limits of multi-agent systems: every task has an indivisible core, splitting it costs an exponential penalty, talking between agents does not pay that penalty back, and only external feedback does.

item.title: How far are we from automating the whole training run?
item.description: Two pipelines taken apart into the steps a person once did by hand, and every method since 2018 placed on the cell it automated. By 2026 what is left for people is judgement, not labour. Interactive: click any cell for the method in symbols and for grandma; pick the axes (time, pipeline stage, compute cost, human cost) to re-plot the field.

item.title: Silicon Samples to Simulate
item.description: An interactive map of 132 papers on LLMs as survey respondents: why the idea took off, six ways it breaks, seven schools of fixes, and why I think SEM is the natural verifier.
